description:
FILED s449 (Fable, round-7 review of agent S).  PRE-EXISTING -- identical on main before S's #550 landed (probed both trees); S's own commit message documents the perl behaviour and the repair simply does not reach digit-named hashes because the container set is punctuation characters.

REPRO (perl 5.40.3):
    sub f {7}
    print "m1=[", f % 3, "]\n";
        perl: prints "m1=[7" and NO closing bracket/newline -- perl reads `%3, "]\n"` as the HASH %3 and both it and the string become f's ARGUMENTS (f ignores them, returns 7)
        PCL:  prints "m1=[1]" -- reads f() % 3 = 1, keeps the "]\n" as print's

The spaced spellings with a real operand (`$x % $y`, `10 % 3`, `f() % 3`, `10 % $h{k}`) are all correct and identical to perl (probed s449).  Only the bareword-callable-then-% shape diverges, and perl's reading needs the WORD to be a list operator still hungry for arguments -- `time % 100` is modulo because time is zero-arity.

Priced low: the shape is pathological (calling f with a hash named %3), occurs in zero population files, and the fix would have to extend `_repair_punct_hash_name`'s set to digit names ONLY in the position where a hungry list operator precedes -- measure whether any real code exists before building that.  The guard rows for #550's set are in Pl/t/punct-array-glob-01.t.
subject: `f % 3` after a DECLARED sub reads as MODULO in PCL where perl reads the hash %3 -- the #550 position rule is right but the punct-container set excludes digit names
